items.title: Why Olipop's founder hasn't sold out to Pepsi or Coca-Cola
items.summary: Not all beverage companies dream of selling out to Big Soda.

items.title: How Olipop is beating big soda at its own game: Fmr CEO
items.summary: Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi sits down with Olipop co-founder and former CEO Ben Goodwin to discuss why traditional full-calorie soda might be a thing of the past, and how Olipop reclaimed the top spot in the category after PepsiCo's acquisition of rival Poppi. Ben Goodwin was still CEO of Olipop at the time of filming.

items.title: 5 High-Yield Dividend Stocks for Retirement Income
items.summary: With Treasury yields near multi-year highs, dividend stocks have to justify their place in a retirement portfolio through more than yield alone. These five names have multi-decade payout track records and live catalysts heading into year-end, but the trade-offs vary sharply.

items.title: The Portfolio Blueprint for Building $19,000 a Month in Dividend Income
items.summary: Generating $19,000 a month from dividends alone sounds like a single problem with one answer, but the yield you chase changes the required nest egg by millions and introduces a completely different set of risks, tax consequences, and long-term tradeoffs.

items.title: 3 Dividend Stocks to Buy Before August Ends and Hold for Life
items.summary: While speculation runs hot and patience gets punished, three Dividend Kings with unbroken raise streaks spanning decades just posted results that made long-term holders take notice, and two of them are sitting at rare discounts heading into September.

items.title: How a 53-Year-Old Can Turn $465,000 Into a Monthly Paycheck Machine by 63
items.summary: Starting yield and dividend growth pull $465,000 in two very different directions over a decade, and choosing the wrong one at 53 could cost you far more than the yield gap suggests.

items.title: How a 77-Year-Old Collects $9,700 a Month Without Selling a Single Share
items.summary: Generating nearly $10,000 a month in retirement income without ever touching principal sounds like a math problem with one answer, but the yield you chase determines whether your portfolio survives the next decade or quietly bleeds out.

items.title: PepsiCo (PEP) Stock May Be 15% Undervalued As Cash Flow Holds Up
items.summary: PepsiCo stock has delivered a decline of about 11.0% over the past three years, yet current valuation work suggests the shares may now trade below a reasonable intrinsic value based on a Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) estimate and earnings multiples. Together these checks point to potential upside relative to the recent share price around US$142.08, even though the broader picture is not a straightforward bargain.
